proposals.evidence: DEDR4572 documents the southern pō-/pōk-/ōg- go family, including Malayalam pōka, Kannada pōgu/hōgu/ōgu and Kota ōg-. These survey pō/ōgu/vōgu/pīge responses compare with that go family and retain source vowels and ordinary endings; no longer auxiliary phrase is included. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5086 gives Tamil mēl/mēlukku/mēkku, Malayalam mēl/mēlē and Kannada mēga/mēle above, higher. These southern survey mel-/mēl-/mēk-/meg- spatial responses retain the attested lateral or velar extensions and ordinary locative endings of the high/above family. Source transcriptions are preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR2668 gives Tamil cutti/cuttiyal, Malayalam cutti/cuttika, Kannada suttige, Tulu sutti/suttè, Telugu sutte and Gondi sutte hammer. These survey cut-/sut- hammer responses retain the attested family and ordinary suffixes. The article also compares Marathi sutkī; this external comparison is retained as a caveat and does not establish an immediate donor for these forms. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR3726 explicitly gives Tamil/Malayalam/Kannada nūl, Tulu/Telugu nūlu, Gadaba/Parji nūl, Gondi nūl and Konda nūlu thread. The survey nūl/nūlu/nol/nōḷ/noolɨ responses are narrowly selected thread reflexes with source vowels and laterals retained; the unrelated crush/broken-rice article3728 is not used. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
